title: Inverse image of set-valued sheaves on small etale sites is exact
statement: Let $h:T'\to T$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. On the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], base change $V\mapsto V\times_TT'$ gives a continuous functor $T_{\Et}\to T'_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous]. Its induced inverse-image functor $h^{-1}:\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\Et})\to\operatorname{Sh}(T'_{\Et})$ on sheaves of sets, left adjoint to $h_*F(V)=F(V\times_TT')$, preserves finite limits and finite colimits; hence this base-change functor defines a morphism of sites $T'_{\Et}\to T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3).

source.place: Lemma Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), assertion (2), and Section Tag 03PZ (section-inverse-image), Definition 59.36.1

proof.text: The base-change functor on small etale sites is continuous, sends coverings to coverings, preserves the relevant fibre products, and its sectionwise direct image on sheaves of sets is a sheaf, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous]. Thus the direct image in the statement is the functor to which the inverse image is adjoint.

The set-valued inverse image is the sheafification of the presheaf pullback along base change. The existing construction [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures] states that this functor is left adjoint to the sectionwise direct image and commutes with finite limits. Therefore it preserves the finite limits asserted in the statement, including the terminal sheaf and binary products.
Since the inverse image is left adjoint to the direct image by Step 2, it preserves all small colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. In particular it preserves finite colimits.

Combining Steps 1–3, the continuous base-change functor has an inverse-image functor preserving finite limits and finite colimits, hence it satisfies the morphism-of-sites condition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3).
